1970.notes: ACIR Significant Features of Fiscal Federalism 1970-71 ed. (M-57), Table 36 (State Individual Income Taxes: Rates, December 31, 1970): Vermont tax = 25% of the federal income tax liability (after retirement income, investment, foreign tax and tax-free covenant bond credits, before other credits and any federal surtax), plus a 15% surcharge for taxable years beginning after December 31, 1968 (25% x 1.15 = 28.75%). Modelled as the 1970 federal schedule x 25% x 1.15 with the federal deduction (federal exemptions; federal percentage standard deduction / low-income allowance as in the federal 1970 entry); federal notes apply (federal surcharge or maximum tax and credits not modelled). The Vermont tax is reduced by the share of AGI that is not Vermont income, and may not exceed the amount that would make combined Vermont and federal liability exceed 4.5% of total income (footnote). Vermont credits (sales tax credit of $0-$81, student credit, property tax credit) not modelled.

1976.notes: ACIR Significant Features of Fiscal Federalism 1976-77 ed. Vol. II, Table 106 (State Individual Income Taxes: Rates, July 1, 1976), Table 107 (personal exemptions, July 1, 1976) and Table 108 (standard deduction, July 1, 1976). Table 106: Vermont tax = 25% of the federal income tax liability (after retirement income, investment, foreign tax and tax-free covenant bond credits, before other credits and federal surtaxes), reduced for non-Vermont income, plus a 9% surcharge. Modelled as the 1976 federal schedule x 25% x 1.09 (= x 0.2725) with the federal deduction (federal $750 exemptions; federal percentage standard deduction 16%, min $1,700/$2,100, max $2,400/$2,800); federal notes apply (general tax credit, 50% maximum tax not modelled). Vermont credits for taxpayers with income under $6,000 not modelled.

1978.notes: Secondary source (Tax Foundation, Facts and Figures on Government Finance, 20th biennial edition 1979, Table 155 'State Individual Income Tax Rates and Related Data', as of September 1, 1978, pp. 192-193; the table credits Commerce Clearing House): footnote u says the Vermont rate applies to federal income tax liability attributable to sources of income within the state and is 25% in Vermont; no surcharge is noted for Vermont (the table notes one for Montana); personal exemptions are the federal exemptions; federal income tax not deductible. Single source; the as-of date falls in 1978, so recorded for tax year 1978. Modelled as the 1978 federal schedule x 25% with the federal deduction (federal $750 exemptions; the zero bracket amount is built into the federal schedule as a 0% first bracket), as in this file's 1980 entry; federal notes apply (general tax credit and 50% maximum tax not modelled). Vermont credits not modelled. The 1979 rate is not stated by any source found: the Book of the States 1980-81 table (as of January 1, 1980) prints 25% while the Joint Fiscal Office history gives 23% for 1980, and the Facts and Figures 1981 table (as of April 1, 1981) gives 23%.
